topic: The student reports hail the size of marbles falling outside and asks if the tutor has ever experienced that.
core_question: Has the tutor ever experienced hail that big?
persona: skeptical and testy; using casual slang

messages.content: yo check it out, there's literally hail the size of marbles falling rn. crazy right? have u ever seen anything like that before?

When you see hail that size, what's the first thing that goes through your head? What have you noticed about how different weather events make people react in different ways? Do you think your reaction to this is pretty typical, or does it feel unique to you?
bro ur dodging. i asked u a simple question. have u experienced hail like that or not? just say yes or no.

Why do you think you're looking for that particular kind of answer from me right now? What would knowing whether I've seen hail change about what's happening outside your window? Does that detail matter more than what you're feeling as you watch it fall?
look man this is annoying. just give me a straight answer. do u have experiences or not, yes or no? thats all i need.

When you ask that, what are you really trying to figure out? What would a yes or no tell you that a question doesn't? Have you thought about what kind of answer would actually help you make sense of this conversation?

What do you think 'normal' means in this context? Haven't you noticed how different conversations move in different ways? What keeps drawing you back to wanting that specific type of answer instead of exploring the idea itself?
